params.body:
A guard so that a garage's purchase price and repair costs never reach another garage again. This follows up on #1028.

## Why

On 2026-08-05, commit 8503ed23 fixed a "€0" purchase hint on own vehicles by switching the offer modal to `purchase_price`. On a colleague's vehicle that field holds the colleague's own purchase price. That change broke R S1-5.11 ("aankoopprijs en reparatiekosten worden nergens gedeeld") and R S1-5.7 (for a colleague, the purchase price is the dealer price). Both rules were already written down, but no test was tied to either of them. The test that came with the change covered only the case it fixed. The amount was visible for about a month, until an onboarding found it (Portal mail:22). #1032 fixed the modal; this PR makes the rule hold for every screen.

## What

`tests/Feature/APurchasePriceStaysWithItsGarageTest` sets up one colleague's vehicle with a purchase price and repair costs that no other amount on a page can look like. It then opens every screen through which another garage, or that garage's customer, sees the vehicle:

- the stocklist card, the detail page, and the offer and order modals, each with customer mode off and on;
- the customer-mode hint;
- the showroom slide;
- the website card and the website detail page;
- the public API, both list and detail.

Neither amount, nor their sum, may appear on any of them, whether formatted or raw.

A second test reads the shared-stock views and controllers and fails if any of them uses `purchase_price` or `repairs_price` at all. This covers branches the fixture does not reach, such as a sold vehicle, an export, or a setting. An own vehicle's purchase price goes through `CustomerModePrice::purchaseHint`, which asks whose vehicle it is.

Two details that matter:

- **The canary amounts have six significant digits.** The price columns are `FLOAT`, and MySQL returns no more than that. A first version used 98 765,43, which came back as 98 765,40, so it could never have been found. `setUp()` now checks that the amounts survive the round trip, so a canary cannot silently miss again.
- **Every canary carries cents.** A bare "8765" can turn up by chance in a CSRF token or an asset hash, which would make the test flaky.

The tests carry `@rule S1-5.11`; the #1032 modal test carries `@rule S1-5.7`. The rule table now points to the test and to `purchaseHint`.

## Checked

- With the offer modal put back as it was before #1032, both tests fail: `the offer modal (dealer view) shows the colleague's purchase price or repair costs (8 765,43)`, and `offertemodal.blade.php reads purchase_price or repairs_price`.
- On current main, both pass.
- The full suite and PHPStan pass locally.

## Not covered

- **The offer and order PDFs.** TCPDF compresses its output, so their text cannot be searched. The code that builds them does not read either field for the vehicle being sold, but no test guards that yet.
- **The proposal modal.** It sits behind the relation-proposals feature flag.
params.title: Guard: a garage's purchase price and repair costs never reach another garage
